It was great to meet with Florida State Representative Adam Anderson to continue our work on the Genomic Answers for Children’s Health Act. I appreciate his leadership at the state level, and I'm proud that our federal legislation builds upon those efforts to help ensure children enrolled in Medicaid who are suspected of having a rare disease or genetic disorder have access to genomic sequencing - a groundbreaking diagnostic tool that has quickly become the standard of care. For far too many families, the search for answers can take years, involving countless medical appointments, unnecessary tests, emotional uncertainty, and significant financial hardship. My Genomic Answers for Children’s Health Act is an important step toward changing that. By expanding access to advanced genomic sequencing and research tools, we can help children receive earlier and more accurate diagnoses, connect them with targeted treatments sooner, and improve health outcomes for those living with rare, complex, and often undiagnosed medical conditions. Every child deserves the opportunity to receive the right diagnosis at the right time, and I look forward to continuing to work with Representative Anderson to advance policies that bring hope and better care to families facing these difficult challenges.

B000490.text: This week, the U.S. House Appropriations Committee debated the final of its 12 annual funding bills. While there was a lot of good in the FY27 Defense funding bill, its lopsided price tag comes at the cost of healthcare, nutrition, housing, and other investments in hardworking Americans here at home. The bill also did not address concerns about Administration’s lack of transparency and accountability to taxpayers. During the debate, I supported an amendment that would require the Defense Department to explain the removal of promoted officers. Our military depends on a promotion system that rewards merit, experience, leadership, and performance. Congress has a responsibility to understand these decisions to maintain confidence in the integrity of the process. Unfortunately, the amendment was not approved and taken together with my other concerns, I could not support this bill as it is currently written. However, I am hopeful that as the House and Senate continue to negotiate a final version, we can craft a better bill that ensures we do right by our servicemembers and military families as well as have the best fighting force defending our country. You can watch my opening remarks during debate on the FY27 Defense funding bill here: https://youtu.be/37E_F_FRe6E

Supporting dairy means supporting farm families, local jobs, school nutrition, rural communities, and Georgia’s agricultural economy.

C001053.text: Terrorists. Cartels. Human traffickers. Drug smugglers. Each day, ICE and Border Patrol agents and officers confront these threats head-on to keep America safe. It’s exactly why I have consistently voted to comprehensively resource these law enforcement professionals as they carry out their security missions. While the far-left hoped to eradicate funding for critical operations and weaken our border security apparatus, House Republicans have made clear that we will continue to support those who defend our homeland and keep our communities safe. That's why we passed the Secure America Act today. However, while I do not regret the objective of our actions today, I am appalled by the complete failure of Senate Democrats that led us to this moment. Chuck Schumer and his radical caucus twice shut down the government, instigating chaos across the nation. Since then, they have continued to diminish Article I and forced the use of reconciliation. It’s wrong – and deliberately undermines the appropriations process. The Constitution entrusts Congress with the power of the purse. Yet, in great irony, the Senate has shown greater concern for protecting an internal rule than fulfilling its constitutional duty. The filibuster is nothing more than an institutional habit. It is neither mentioned nor sanctioned in our founding documents. I would remind my peers on the other side of the Rotunda that no chamber precedent is greater than the bedrock of our Republic. Members swear an oath to uphold the Constitution – not the filibuster. I thoroughly regret the erosion of Article I authority that Senate Democrats have instigated, and the price everyday Americans have been forced to pay as a result. I hope the months-long charade that led us to this moment serves as a reminder that no partisan fixation is worth shutting down the government, abandoning constitutional responsibilities, and forcing Congress into extraordinary measures simply to perform its most basic duties. I believe in the Constitution, the power of the purse, and completing the appropriations process. I also believe in keeping the homeland safe. The Senate may have abandoned proper governing, but I will not abandon those who stand watch over our borders and protect our communities. Our work, of course, doesn’t end here. As the Fiscal Year 2027 Appropriations markups near completion, I am reminded that governing is a choice. The work I do, the votes I cast, and the actions I take will always be guided by one principle: fulfilling our obligations to the American people

For 39 years, Governor Bill Anoatubby has led my tribe, the Chickasaw Nation, with remarkable vision, a strategic hand, and unwavering dedication. His leadership has transformed not only the trajectory of the Nation, but the lives of the Chickasaw people.   Economically, his tenure has been nothing short of historic and unprecedented. Through Governor Anoatubby’s steady leadership, the Chickasaw Nation did more than just achieve its goals of economic development and self-sufficiency – it surpassed them. Under his guidance, the tribe evolved from dependence on federal funding to one that is self-sufficient and prosperous on its own. Today, thanks to him, the Chickasaw Nation supports more than 22,000 jobs and contributes $3.7 billion annually to Oklahoma’s economy, including $1.2 billion in wages and benefits.   However, Governor Anoatubby’s impact cannot be measured by just economics. Throughout his lengthy tenure, he also placed a significant emphasis on preserving and sharing the precious heritage of the Chickasaw Nation. Through initiatives such as the Chickasaw Nation Division of Arts and Humanities and the Chickasaw Cultural Center, he ensured that our history, language, arts, and culture would continue to inspire future generations.   These achievements, on top of many others, make it unmistakably clear: Governor Bill Anoatubby is the most consequential Chickasaw Nation leader since the removal period. And his influence has extended past just the Chickasaw Nation. His leadership and impact are respected by every Oklahoman.   For nearly four decades, Governor Anoatubby has embodied true commitment to the Chickasaw people and Oklahoma. The powerful combination of his leadership, vision, and generosity has allowed all of us in our state to shape a brighter future for ourselves and all those touched by the results of his leadership. On a personal level, I am fortunate to call Governor Anoatubby a mentor and a trusted friend.   His retirement is an enormous loss for the Chickasaw Nation, all Indian Country, and the state of Oklahoma. However, he leaves the tribe stronger than he found it, as he hands it off to his very competent and bright son, Chris, the Lieutenant Governor. I have no doubt Chris will carry on his father’s legacy with wisdom, competence, and care, and I look forward to seeing everything the future holds for the Chickasaw Nation.   In conclusion, to Governor Anoatubby, congratulations on a truly remarkable career and a lifetime of service. Thank you for your leadership, your vision, your friendship, and the legacy you leave behind. I wish you, Janice, and your entire family the best as you enter this next chapter.

M000312.text: 81 years ago today, representatives of 50 countries gathered in San Francisco to sign the U.N. Charter. I am proud that U.N. Charter was signed in the United States. I am proud that so many Americans have fought for a country that stands up for human rights and lives up to the ideals embedded in our founding. The United Nations was a direct response to the horrors of the Second World War. Having witnessed the systematic murder of six million Jews and millions of others, the destruction of entire cities, and the deaths of tens of millions of civilians, the people of the world resolved to build a global system to "save succeeding generations from the scourge of war" and "reaffirm faith in fundamental human rights, in the dignity and worth of the human person." Sadly, right now, we are moving in the wrong direction. Protecting human dignity requires honoring our legal commitments under the U.N. Charter and U.N. human rights treaties. The United States is a party to three: the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, the Convention Against Torture, and the International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination. W000821.text: Arkansas, and the United States, have an incredibly abundant source of timber. With a background in Forestry and Engineering, Congressman Westerman understands just how important our pulp and paper industry is and he remains heavily focused on legislation that will support such an important economic contributer for Arkansas. F000466.text: Today would have been my big brother Mike’s 63rd birthday. Mike was the kind of man whose absence is felt so deeply because his presence meant so much. He was steady, selfless, faithful, and good—a leader in our family, a servant to our community, and an example to all of us blessed to know and love him. To know Mike Fitzpatrick was to know a friend. A true friend. He had a way of showing up for people—quietly, consistently, completely. He believed in doing the work, keeping your word, and leaving things better than you found them. He was more than my big brother. He was the man I looked up to, learned from, and still try to honor in how I live and serve. He is so missed—in the big moments, the quiet ones, and in all the spaces his love once filled. Today, we hold my sister-in-law, nieces and nephews, and entire family especially close, and give thanks for Mike’s life, his love, and the legacy that still lights the way.

RT by @RepBrianFitz: The most remarkable story of redemption I came across in my years writing Courage Can Save US. “If I put on one hand the people I care most about in this world,” ex-convict, former NY State Assemblyman, and onetime prospective candidate for Mayor of NYC Brian McLaughlin told me early one morning in 2025 at a Starbucks in Manhattan. It had been nearly 19 years since then Special Agent Brian Fitzpatrick put McLaughlin behind bars, ending his political career and beginning a chapter of covert cooperation with the FBI that would eventually help bring down Sheldon Silver, the powerful Speaker of the New York State Assembly, and scores of others across organized crime and politics. “There’s my mutha, my fatha, my brutha, my kids, and there’s Brian Fitzpatrick.”

Nearly twenty years ago, Brian McLaughlin and I met under circumstances neither of us could have imagined would one day lead to friendship. I was a young FBI Special Agent in New York City, working my first field assignment. Brian was the Subject of the FBI public corruption case I was assigned to investigate. He was ultimately arrested, convicted, and sentenced to ten years in prison. That is where many people would have ended the story. But our country, at its best, has always believed in something larger than a person’s worst chapter. It believes in accountability, but also in redemption. It believes in consequences, but also in grace. It believes that lives can be rebuilt when truth is faced with courage. Last night, I had the honor of sitting down with Brian—now my friend, and someone who attended my wedding just last weekend—to tell that story together. Brian has said that I changed his life. The truth is, he changed mine, too. Thank you to my friend, @WithHonorAction Founder @ryebarcott , for profiling me in your inspiring new book. Courage can, in fact, save us.

This month is Gun Violence Awareness Month, and the numbers tell a story we cannot keep accepting. Gun violence is the leading cause of death for children and teens in this country. Not car accidents. Not illness. Guns.      We say we want safer schools, safer communities, and a better future for our kids. Today, the Department of the Interior announced Payments in Lieu of Taxes (PILT) funding for 2025, with Idaho receiving $43 million. PILT is a critically important program that rural communities across the Gem State depend on because 62% of the land within our borders is owned and managed by the federal government. For the last six years, I have worked as a mom and a member of the >@EnergyCommerce Committee to protect children online. With the bipartisan KIDS Act, we have a real chance to notch a win in that fight. I commend Ranking Member @FrankPallone for his diligence and persistence in negotiating the strongest compromise possible on an issue that is as urgent as it is difficult. Like any compromise, the KIDS Act isn’t perfect. I’ve heard from parents and advocates who believe Congress should go further, and I agree with much of what they’re asking for. But we cannot tell children and families to wait until Democrats retake power in Washington to act, not when real progress is sitting right in front of us. The protections we win today have to actually hold. Provisions that sound strong but get struck down in court tomorrow don’t keep a single kid safer. This agreement is built to survive, and that matters. I’m proud to support the KIDS Act, and I’m just as committed to what comes next. I will keep fighting for every tool parents need to hold Big Tech accountable and for every protection our children deserve.

Thank you to the entire staff and team @hospitals4kids for your dedication and partnership.  I’ll always fight to ensure every child in Massachusetts and across the nation can access the quality, lifesaving care they need.

For decades, NIH-funded research has unlocked treatments and advanced work toward cures for cancer, Alzheimer's, diabetes and countless other conditions that devastate American families. That progress depends on scientists, not politicians, deciding which research holds the most promise. Now, Donald Trump wants to put himself in charge of which grants get funded. That means the next breakthrough could die because it didn't serve his agenda. I worked with @RepRaskin and @RepDelBene to demand this Administration reverse course and end this war on science. Families are depending on this lifesaving research.

Now the Trump administration is deciding company by company who gets access to the newest AI model. No law. No process. No oversight. Just appointees in Washington deciding who's in and who's out.  This haphazard approach is bad for safety, national security, and American innovation. Congress can't keep sitting on the sidelines of the AI debate.  We need a real national strategy. Agencies staffed with technical experts, uniform guardrails for frontier models, and a lawful process for emergency action that answers to judicial review.

S001215.text: June is National Homeownership Month. As Trump refuses to make housing more affordable, too many Michiganders are being locked out of homeownership. My Homeownership Savings Act will help more Michigan families save, buy a home, and build wealth. Let's get it passed.

I’m not a millionaire, and I haven't used my time in elected office to get rich. But that is not true for everyone. My “Release Your Taxes Act” would make all Members of Congress and candidates for Congress follow in my lead and release their tax returns.
When Michigan is in a moment of uncertainty or crisis, I'm running toward it. I did it then during the Obama auto rescue, and I've done it every day since.

This week, Democrats and Republicans came together to pass a major bill to make it easier to buy a home, build more housing in America, and crack down on private equity buying up houses. But today, for purely political reasons, Trump refused to sign it. Everywhere I go across Michigan, I hear about the high cost of housing and how we need to make homeownership easier. I’ve been a proud supporter of this bill and even introduced my own legislation to reduce financial barriers to homeownership for Michiganders. Donald Trump has once again proven that he doesn’t care about Americans’ cost-of-living issues. Trump must sign this bill to lower housing costs, NOW.
I’ve stood with Michigan autoworkers my entire career. Last month, I was back on the ground with them, and now I’m back in Congress pushing harder than ever for the support they deserve.

Supporting farmers whose crops were destroyed by early spring freeze, rolling back President Trump’s harmful tariffs, and investing proactively in outbreak prevention – these are the solutions our agriculture industry, and our entire community, need. P.S. Want to hear more about my time in our district last week? You can read my latest newsletter (and sign up for future updates) at the link in my bio.

M001204.text: In 2025, Small Business Investment Companies (SBICs) delivered more than $53 billion in investment capital to small businesses nationwide. Over the past two decades, businesses backed by SBICs created 3 million new jobs and supported an additional 10.5 million jobs. Last month, President Trump signed my Investing in All of America Act into law, legislation that will increase the capital available to small businesses, especially those in rural and underserved communities, manufacturing, or the critical technology sector through SBICs. In this week’s @HouseSmallBiz Committee hearing, I asked Joshua Carter, Associate Administrator for the @SBAgov’s Office of Investment and Innovation, about this success and how this new law is allowing the SBA to support more small businesses and crucial industries. I appreciate my counterpart on the other side of the aisle, @RepScholten, for helping me get this overwhelmingly bipartisan bill signed into law. Our work together is proof that both parties can come together to deliver real solutions to the American people. Watch our remarks:

It’s simple: only American citizens should be voting in American elections. That’s why the @HouseGOP passed the SAVE America Act to secure our elections and preserve American democracy. Now, it’s time for the Senate to rally around commonsense voter ID legislation. Watch my interview this morning with @MariaBartiromo on @FoxBusiness, where I emphasize the need for Congress to break the legislative logjam, recap President Trump’s recent event at the Mack Truck plant in Pennsylvania, and discuss my recent meeting with new Federal Reserve Chairman, Kevin Warsh.

I will be joining Mornings with Maria tomorrow at 6:20 AM to discuss Republicans’ plans to continue delivering for the American people and President Trump’s visit to Pennsylvania this week. Make sure to tune in.

It was great to welcome ELCO High School senior Lila Leisey of Lebanon County to my office in Washington to congratulate her on winning the Ninth Congressional District’s 2026 Congressional Art Competition. Lila’s winning entry, entitled “Keystone State,” is a 12-by-12 watercolor painting featuring a Pennsylvania Dutch quilt pattern with prints of the Liberty Bell. This year’s competition theme, America 250, encouraged students to celebrate the 250th anniversary of our nation’s founding. I can think of no better artwork to represent our district than a rendering that features Independence Hall’s iconic bell. Her artwork will hang in the U.S. Capitol for the next year for members of Congress, staff, and visitors to admire. Congratulations, Lila, on this well-deserved honor.

This week, I appreciated the opportunity to travel back from President Trump’s event in Macungie with the President, @SenMcCormickPA, and @RepMackenzie. We had productive conversations about Pennsylvania, our economy, energy, manufacturing, and what more can be done to create jobs and strengthen our Commonwealth. One thing is always clear when you’re with President Trump: he’s constantly asking what more can be done for Pennsylvania and for the American people. His focus is on restoring American strength, expanding opportunity, and ensuring our nation’s best days are still ahead. It was also an honor to join President Trump for the kickoff of the Great American State Fair on the National Mall as we begin celebrating America’s 250th anniversary. It was a fitting way to celebrate our nation’s remarkable history while continuing to work toward an even brighter future. God Bless America! 🇺🇸

Last week, I joined @MyFDOT Secretary Perdue and his team at SunTrax in Auburndale for an update on Florida's Advanced Air Mobility initiatives and a look at the work underway to keep our state at the forefront of aviation innovation. SunTrax has become a national leading test site for next-generation transportation. From electric aircraft and vertiports to the aerial corridors that could connect communities across Central Florida. While many states are still discussing these concepts, Florida is actively building the infrastructure, partnerships and regulatory framework needed to make them a reality. Central Florida is uniquely positioned to lead in this emerging industry thanks to its strong aviation ecosystem, world-class research institutions and growing transportation network. The investments being made today have the potential to create high-skilled jobs, attract new businesses and strengthen our region's role as a national center for aerospace and transportation innovation. As Co-Chair of the Advanced Air Mobility Caucus and a member of @HouseAppropsGOP, I've worked to support these efforts, including securing funding for AAM infrastructure and projects in FL-18. The technologies being developed today will help shape the future of transportation, expand economic opportunities and keep Florida at the forefront of aviation for years to come.

The federal government should live within its means, just like hardworking American families do. I'll keep fighting to protect economic liberty, eliminate waste, fraud, and abuse, and ensure Americans keep more of what they earn.

On this day in history in 1963, President John F. Kennedy delivered his iconic "Ich bin ein Berliner,” or “I am a Berliner,” speech in West Berlin during the Cold War. Speaking to a crowd of West Germans, Kennedy offered a powerful show of support amid tensions surrounding the newly built Berlin Wall. His message declared West Berlin a symbol of freedom. L000599.text: Doina and I are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Lauren Shields of Rockland County, and we offer our deepest condolences to her family and friends. Lauren was the definition of a fighter. At just 26 years old, she accomplished more than most do in an entire lifetime. She received a life-saving heart transplant at just 8 years old and, in 2020, a kidney transplant from her mother - two extraordinary gifts that allowed her to dedicate her life to helping others. A proud graduate of Albertus Magnus High School and Dominican University, Lauren became a passionate advocate for organ donation. She helped inspire the passage of Lauren’s Law in New York, encouraging more people to register as organ donors. Lauren went on to serve as a Community and Government Affairs Liaison with LiveOnNY, advocating for the thousands of New Yorkers still waiting for a lifesaving transplant. I had the honor of knowing Lauren and considered her a friend. I can say without a doubt that Lauren made the Hudson Valley a better place, and she will be deeply missed.

RT by @RepDeluzio: We spoke with @RepDeluzio about the Let Kids Play Act 🏛️ The bill wants to keep private equity out of youth sports. One of the most interesting moments from our conversation wasn't about PE. But growth capital. We surveyed nearly 180 youth sports operators and one result stood out: 75% said they aren't looking to sell their business. They're not looking for an exit. They're looking for a partner. And most importantly keep control of the business they built. @KyleScottL asked Congressman Deluzio how the Let Kids Play Act addresses those operators, his response was notable, "If you're retaining control and you're talking about passive investment to open up the capital you might need to make an expansion, that feels maybe a little different than when you've got control and you're engaging in these practices that we see. That feels like a very different kind of investment, perhaps. And so maybe the devil's in the details there. I see the need on the privately owned facilities. I see how that investment might make sense. And we should dig in on that too." He acknowledged there's a difference between passive investment that helps an owner grow and investment tied to the business practices the bill seeks to eliminate. While also recognizing that youth sports needs capital both private and public. It'll be interesting to how this bill advances and what mark ups could be made to protect smaller operators looking to expand while maintaining control of the business. #youthsports

Investing in cutting-edge technology, strengthening our wildfire preparedness, and improving forest management must remain national priorities. Thank you to the #GlobalSumudFlotilla —including an individual from the East Bay who is traveling on the flotilla—for leading a peaceful humanitarian mission to end man-made famine and genocide in Gaza. I urge the Israeli government to end the blockade and let desperately needed humanitarian aid in immediately.

The Trump administration is using confidential data collected by federal agencies to racially profile immigrant communities. My district is one of the most diverse places in the country, and in CA-12 we don’t stand by while our neighbors are harassed, terrorized, and illegally detained. That’s why I’m cosponsoring the Home Together Act and the Limiting ICE’s National Encroachment Act to reign this administration in. CA-12 says not in our neighborhood.

Last week, Ms. Harjit Kaur —a member of the Hercules community for over 30 years who spent years working at Sari Palace in Berkeley— was detained by ICE officials.    Ms. Kaur is a mother, grandmother, and beloved member of her community. Her detention is yet another example of the Trump Administration’s callous campaign against immigrants. She has reported to ICE every six months and has no criminal record -- the point is cruelty.    I join @RepGaramendi, who represents Ms. Kaur, in calling for the safe release of our Bay Area neighbor.

G000605.text: Team Gray joined members of the Fresno Irrigation District for the ribbon-cutting ceremony celebrating the completion of the Carter-Bybee Basin Groundwater Recharge Basin. This project will help strengthen groundwater supplies and improve long-term water reliability for communities across #CA13.

Army Sergeant Alan Frunz earned the Purple Heart in 1968 but never received the medal. Nearly six decades later, working with the U.S. Army, my office helped ensure Sergeant Frunz finally received the recognition he earned through his service and sacrifice.
In Modesto, we brought together local labor leaders and organizers to discuss how we can work together to support folks across #CA13.

Antojitos Sinaloa brings authentic flavors and a welcoming community atmosphere to #CA13. Already known for its food truck at Grub Hub Modesto, Team Gray was onsite to celebrate the grand opening of its new storefront on Carpenter Road.
Team Gray was in Modesto for the American Graffiti Festival & Car Show. A great event to support children and youth in our community.

L000607.text: This week’s Supreme Court decision allows the Trump administration to end Temporary Protected Status for more than 356,000 Haitians and Syrians living in the United States, despite the fact that many would suffer political persecution and even death if returned involuntarily.  In the face of Trumpian cruelty and chaos, Congress must act to create life-saving pathways.

On #EqualityDay, we celebrate the anniversary of Obergefell v. Hodges, the Supreme Court decision that secured marriage equality nationwide. We honor the advocates, couples, & communities who fought for that victory & continue the work to protect equal rights for every LGBTQ+ American
JD is right: compared to Trump, Nixon wasn’t so bad…
This is the least productive Congress in modern history, so hitting singles is significant.
If you’re rooting for Balogun and the rest of the US team, you should root for birthright citizenship.

W000830.text: It was great talking with @Astros4America, an incredible organization of over 100 former NASA astronauts coming together to support America’s constitutional democracy. As NASA's former chief of staff, I know firsthand how deeply these men and women love America. We spoke about the importance of their shared mission, to uphold constitutional principles and to support leaders who demonstrate commitment to those principles and the ability to work across differences to solve problems. They are focused on protecting American constitutional democracy for the long term—beyond any election cycle. Check out their web page at https://www.astronautsforamerica.org/

It’s shocking but true: we do not know what AI is doing to our kids’ ability to think. But it’s already being put into the classroom. We need to understand the impacts of AI on students before we let a whole generation fall behind.

I met with Neighborhood Legal Services of Los Angeles County, the only legal aid organization serving the Antelope Valley, to talk about the free legal assistance they provide to residents in our area who need it most. We discussed how we can work together to support our neighbors facing housing, consumer protection, and other legal challenges.

American innovation depends on investing in the scientists and researchers who drive discovery. But the Trump Administration has given out 60-70% fewer grant awards than in previous years, threatening critical research and putting our global competitiveness at risk. Now is the time we should be strengthening America's research enterprise, not undermining it.

The largest bipartisan housing bill in decades was supposed to be signed into law today. Instead, the President put it on hold. As so many Americans know, we're facing a housing affordability crisis that can't wait. Mr. President, sign the Road to Housing Act into law immediately.

R000620.text: ICYMI: I called out Republicans for threatening to sink a bill because of my data centers amendment. My amendment would have helped us understand energy and water use at data centers – an issue that is important for our constituents. Republicans are silencing the needs of our constituents. https://rollcall.com/2026/06/26/federal-ai-security-center-measure-advanced-by-house-science/

Introducing our CA-29 Congressional Art Competition winner, Pettik from Valley Glen! I met with Pettik and his family were in Washington this week to see his piece – Music Along the Way – be unveiled in the U.S. Capitol, where it will be on display for the next year. Congratulations Pettik!

RT by @RepLuzRivas: Today, we celebrate the anniversary of Obergefell v. Hodges which legalized same-sex marriage. Love is love, and everyone deserves the right to marry who they wish. The fight continues to ensure full equality for the LGBTQ community.

With the over $1,000,000 in federal funding I secured for CSUN’s Autodesk Technology Engagement Center, students will have access to new cutting edge technology, research equipment, and STEM learning opportunities. Thank you to @csunorthridge and President Beck for their partnership in helping expand educational STEM opportunities for students across the San Fernando Valley. Read the full article here: https://sanfernandosun.com/2026/06/24/congresswoman-luz-rivas-presents-over-1m-in-funding-for-stem-center-at-csun/

WATCH: I called out Republicans in our Science, Space, and Technology hearing. 👀 Republicans THREATENED to pull a bill I had an amendment on water and energy use at data centers. They also flat out rejected another amendment of mine that would provide multilingual materials for AI literacy and education because they thought it was "DEI." Members are elected to vote. There should be no hiding, no threats to pull bills, and no silencing our constituents. Period.

F000483.text: R to @RepFriedmanCA: Small businesses like K’arsi are what makes CA-30 not only a foodie’s delight, but an honor to represent in Congress. Their stories of resilience and success inspire me every day.

What’s better than one K’arsi? Two K’arsis! The Armenian family behind the beloved Glendale bakery just opened their second location in downtown Burbank, which I got to visit. Whether you love lavash or just want to explore the magical world of Armenian pastries, K’arsi is the place to go.

57 years ago today, LGBTQ Americans and their allies fought back at Stonewall, ushering in a new dawn for LGBTQ visibility and rights across the country. This year, when those same rights are under attack, let’s pledge to never go back to those dark days.

As Congress’ unofficial Thrifting and Vintage Ambassador, it’s my privilege to highlight businesses that help upcycle beautiful treasures from yesteryear for today’s generations. Junk for Joy has been doing that for 50 years. I stopped by to recognize them for their decades of bringing joy to CA-30 (and did a little browsing while I was there).

I represent a community of creators and artists in my district, so I understand exactly how important it is to have control over your own voice and image. With the advancement of AI, we need new laws for new realities. I’m proud to be an early champion of the NO FAKES Act, a bipartisan and bicameral bill that will give Americans a powerful tool to protect themselves from scammers and bad actors using AI.

H001100.text: Today, I spoke with local, county, state, and federal officials, including Governor Polis, regarding the ongoing response to the fires across Western Colorado. I appreciate the close coordination among our local, state, and federal partners as they work to protect lives, property, and our communities. Our hearts remain with the families of the three firefighters who lost their lives, the two firefighters who were injured, and the entire wildland firefighting community during this incredibly difficult time. For the latest information on active fires and fire conditions, Watch Duty is a helpful public resource: https://app.watchduty.org/ For official evacuation, pre-evacuation, road closure, and emergency notices, please sign up for alerts from your local sheriff’s office and emergency management agency, and continue to follow their official updates.

I am saddened by the deaths of the three firefighters who were killed while responding to the Knowles and Gore Fires along the Colorado-Utah border. Wildland firefighting is among the most demanding and dangerous forms of public service. These brave men and women willingly put themselves in harm’s way to protect our communities, our public lands, and one another. My prayers are with the families and loved ones of those who were killed, the two firefighters who were injured, and the entire wildland firefighting community as they mourn this tragic loss. We are deeply grateful for the courage, service, and sacrifice of all who answer this call.

What makes a rural town grow? In Delta, it's small businesses, a thriving Main Street, outdoor recreation, and the public lands that bring visitors from across the country. But none of that happens by accident. I joined Delta County Commissioner Craig Fuller, Mayor Ron White, Council Member Janet Rowland, and local business owners to talk about how we can help Delta continue to grow. We discussed supporting Delta’s Main Street revitalization, expanding recreation opportunities, and ensuring reliable energy remains part of Delta's future.  When local leaders, business owners, and government work together, communities like Delta are well positioned to create jobs, attract investment, and build opportunity for the next generation. #CO03 #DeltaCounty

America needs more energy, not less, and #CO03 is uniquely positioned to help lead the way. Today, we have an opportunity not only to meet America’s growing energy needs, but to strengthen our allies, support innovation, create good-paying jobs, and reinforce our economic and national security. That was the focus of the JOLT Energy Summit in Grand Junction, where leaders from across the country came together to discuss how we can remove barriers to responsible energy development and unleash American ingenuity.  It was also great to welcome Karen Budd-Falen from the Department of the Interior to Colorado’s Third District. Together, we can help ensure Colorado remains a leader in responsible energy production for decades to come. #MesaCounty

Reliable, affordable propane helps keep Western and Southern Colorado moving. From powering irrigation pumps and drying crops to heating homes, fueling small businesses, and supporting ranching operations, propane plays an important role in communities across #CO03. It was great to meet with members of the Colorado Propane Gas Association, including Skotty and Audra Morris of La Jara, to hear firsthand about the opportunities and challenges facing the industry. Conversations with local business owners and energy producers help ensure the policies we pursue in Washington support the jobs, families, and rural economies that make Colorado's Third District strong.

C001137.text: Congratulations to Caleb from The Vanguard School on winning this year's Congressional Art Competition for #CO05! His artwork, “Canterbury Cathedral,” is now displayed in the halls of the U.S. Capitol, where it will be viewed by thousands of visitors from across the globe.

✅PASSED: Financial Exploitation Prevention Act   The financial exploitation of our seniors and retirees needs to stop. Since 2020, reported financial fraud losses among Americans age 60 and older have quadrupled. This bill protects seniors from financial fraud by providing new tools for investment companies to temporarily delay suspicious withdrawals so they can verify the transaction with the account holder before the money is lost.

Thanks to the Colorado Contractors Association for coming to our DC office to discuss issues facing the industry, including the burdensome regulations that make it harder to keep construction costs down. I have introduced the FRAMER Act to combat overly strict state energy mandates, making it easier for Americans to achieve homeownership.

Last evening, I joined the University of Colorado's CU in DC conference to welcome students and faculty to our nation's capital. Our students are the future of our nation, and it was nice to discuss issues important to them and take questions regarding Colorado and current issues our nation is facing.

The House just passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which now heads to the @POTUS’ desk to be signed into law.   The American dream of homeownership is out of reach for many. By passing this bill, we are working towards tackling affordability by reducing regulation and increasing the housing supply, making it easier for Americans across the country to own a home.

E000300.text: Federal agencies shouldn't keep taxpayers waiting for money they're owed. Our office has been working with a constituent since April to resolve issues related to her delayed 2024 and 2025 tax refunds. While her 2025 refund was released separately, her 2024 refund remained on hold. After coordinating with the appropriate agency, our office successfully helped remove the hold and secure the release of her $7,874 tax refund. Helping constituents navigate federal agencies and cut through bureaucratic delays is one of the most important services our office provides. If you are experiencing issues with a federal agency, my office is here to help!

RT by @repgabeevans: One provision in the Working Families Tax Cut is bringing 30,000 housing units to Colorado. @repgabeevans joins @kr_bledsoe to discuss what putting money back in people's pockets actually looks like.

RT by @repgabeevans: During yesterday’s Energy Subcommittee markup, @RepGabeEvans' Ratepayer Protection Act was forwarded to the full committee for consideration. This represents the first step in advancing this key legislation that protects all Americans as we continue to secure our grid, lower prices, and win the race for AI.

RT by @repgabeevans: West Texas families, agricultural producers, and small businesses should not be forced to subsidize costs for data centers. If data centers and large new energy loads require new infrastructure to be built, the companies driving that demand should be the ones paying for it. That's why I spoke in favor of the Ratepayer Protection Act by @RepGabeEvans. We want America to lead the world in AI, but winning the race cannot come at the expense of American taxpayers.

RT by @repgabeevans: Today, the Committee advanced @RepGabeEvans’ legislation to streamline offices within DHS’s Office of Intelligence and Analysis (I&A), which would enhance the Department’s coordination with state & local law enforcement: “I was a cop for a little over 10 years in the Denver metro area, and so I know there’s nothing more critical to law enforcement operations than communication between local, state, and federal agencies.”

H001099.text: I spent the afternoon at the University of Central Florida meeting with professors, students, university leadership, and private sector partners to discuss workforce development, defense research, and the role higher education plays in strengthening our nation's competitiveness. UCF continues to be a leader in innovation and is helping prepare the next generation of scientists, engineers, and skilled professionals who will drive America's future.

The Indian River Lagoon is one of our region's greatest natural treasures, and protecting it remains a top priority. It was great to visit Spoonbill Marsh and announce $1 million in federal funding for the Ixora Park Septic-to-Sewer Conversion Project, an important investment that will help improve water quality and reduce pollution entering the Lagoon for years to come.

Keeping families safe starts with smart infrastructure investments. It was great meeting with Brightline to discuss the safety upgrades being implemented across the Space Coast and Treasure Coast to improve crossing awareness, increase visibility, and enhance public safety for everyone who travels through our communities.

Manufacturing matters. I appreciated the opportunity to tour Jaycon's facility and learn more about the cutting-edge work they're doing in electronics manufacturing and emerging technologies. Expanding American manufacturing strengthens our economy and supports our national security. 🇺🇸

The future of our community is bright because of outstanding young men and women like those recognized at this year's Medal of Merit ceremony. Congratulations to all of the recipients. Your hard work, leadership, character, and commitment to serving others does not go unnoticed. I look forward to seeing all they accomplish in the years ahead.

J000311.text: On this day in 1944, over 34,000 American soldiers crowded together in small, amphibious boats en route to Omaha Beach. As the boats landed on the beach, and their bow ramps dropped down leading the men ashore, unrelenting machine gun fire rained down from enemy bunkers. Undeterred, the American and Allied forces emerged from the battle victorious, but not without a heavy cost. Over 2,500 Americans died at Omaha Beach. One of them was 1st Lieutenant Thomas Royce Dallas Jr. from our Congressional District in Griffin, Georgia, who drew his last breath on the shores of Omaha Beach. As we remember the heroism Americans exhibited on D-Day and we reflect on the cost of freedom, may we remember and be inspired by the names and faces of those brave soldiers who died in service to our Country.

RT by @RepBrianJack: Federal defense contracts meant for small businesses are being SWEPT UP by large corporations. WATCH: @RepBrianJack and Mr. Jaworowski break down how strengthening the Rule of Two could give Main Street a fighting chance.

Today, we fully reopened the Tyrone Post Office! Before I was sworn into Congress, I promised to reopen the Tyrone Post Office, which had previously suffered extensive structural damage due to a fire.  As of today, the Tyrone Post Office is fully open for business. During a Congressional oversight hearing, I asked the Postmaster General to accelerate the Post Office’s reconstruction, which had been delayed for years.  He and his team swiftly reacted, and worked closely with my team to achieve this goal. Thank you to Tyrone Mayor Eric Dial and the Tyrone Town Council for your partnership and forceful advocacy, and thank you to Postmaster General David Steiner, and Kayla Dufrene, Brandy Jackson, and Sharon Alston of the Postal Service for your leadership on this important project.

Tonight, I was honored to partner with the @GoClingstones and host a Service Academy Night at the ballpark for six of the outstanding students I appointed to our country’s military service academies.  Sadly, the game was eventually rained out, but the fans were uplifted, as each appointee walked on the field with their families to be individually recognized on the jumbotron for their patriotism. As we reflect this week on the costly sacrifices made to defend our freedom, we are inspired by these young men and women preparing to attend the United States Military Academy at West Point, the United States Naval Academy at Annapolis, and the United States Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs. Congratulations to Addison, Colson, Mahika, Matthew, Steven, and Travonte!

This morning, I was honored to join Coweta County veterans, families, and community leaders at Newnan’s Memorial Day Ceremony. Newnan is a community from which heroes are born.  Two of Georgia’s 27 Medal of Honor recipients were from Newnan, and dozens more have earned a Purple Heart.  At today’s ceremony, we honored one of those recipients, Private First Class James Alfred “Alf” Smith, a Newnan native, who was posthumously awarded the Purple Heart after sacrificing his life in service to our country during World War I. May the stories of these heroes continue to inspire us and the next generation of guardians of our freedom.

S001229.text: Good to welcome @IndianaChamber CEO Vanessa Sinders to our office this week. For more than a century, the Indiana Chamber has been a leading voice for Hoosier jobs and a stronger, pro-growth economy. We talked through priorities shaping Indiana’s business climate — and how my work from Washington can help keep Indiana competitive. Businesses invest in Indiana — because they know Hoosiers are ready to work!

The first piece Annika Pentecost ever entered into an art competition now hangs in the U.S. Capitol. It was a pleasure to host Annika and her mom at this year’s Congressional Art Competition. The Northeastern High School sophomore won the #IN06 competition with Jefferson Memorial, a striking nighttime piece inspired by her school’s trip to Washington. Her artwork will be on display in the Capitol for the year ahead. Congratulations, Annika!

Good meeting with Hoosier nurses from #IN06 and @ANANursingWorld to discuss our nursing workforce, patient access, and the health care needs facing Indiana families. Nurses play a central role in maternal health, veterans’ health, mental health, and public health. I appreciate Amy Engle and Emily Sego taking the time to share their perspective and advocacy.

A major milestone tonight: We’ve now advanced all twelve appropriations bills out of committee, with two already passed by the full House. Over the past couple of months, we’ve spent long days and late nights working to make sure taxpayer dollars are spent wisely. Moving these bills forward on time is a return to regular order. It’s how Congress is supposed to work. As the first Indiana Republican to serve on Appropriations in 30 years, I was able to help advance priorities that matter to Indiana. The work isn’t finished. These bills now continue through the House and Senate process. Getting our fiscal house back in order starts with doing the basics well.

We got to work this morning on the final markup of the appropriations season: Defense. We’ll run late into the evening — because this bill matters to Hoosiers and to every American family. It supports our troops, strengthens our military readiness, and helps keep our country safe. That’s serious work — and we’re treating it that way.

S001228.text: Great meeting with the Kansas State Nurses Association to discuss strengthening the nursing workforce, expanding access to care, and supporting priorities, including maternal health, veterans' health, mental health, and more. Thank you to Kansas nurses for sharing your insights and for the essential care nurses provide to our communities every day.

Thank you to the Kansas Music Educators Association for stopping by my office to discuss education priorities affecting music programs across our state. I appreciate your advocacy and dedication to supporting music education for kids in Kansas schools and communities.

Enjoyed meeting with Leo Norman, this year's Congressional Art Competition winner and a recent graduate of Pittsburg High School. The Congressional Art Competition is a nationwide contest that recognizes and encourages the artistic talent of high school students across the country. Leo's outstanding artwork will be displayed in the U.S. Capitol for the next year, representing Kansas’s second district. Congratulations, Leo, on this well-deserved achievement!

Had a great meeting with Kansans active with the American Horse Council to discuss important issues affecting horses and the people who care for them. We talked about protecting horses from abuse, addressing veterinarian shortages, updating import rules for competition horses, and preparing for animal health threats like screwworm. Thank you for the thoughtful discussion and for your continued support of America's horse industry.
RT by @RepDerekSchmidt: The House passed the bipartisan Main Street Competes Act https://www.c-span.org/clip/us-house-of-representatives/user-clip-hr-8882-main-street-competes-act/5201812

O000176.text: This is a Supreme Court that has dismantled decades of precedent. Justices serve for life with little accountability. My ROBE Act would establish 18-year term limits for Supreme Court justices.

No child should have to worry about where their next meal is coming from. #TeamMD02 was proud to join @NoKidHungryMD to kick off their summer meals program. Through @bcplinfo branches, children across our community can access free meals all summer long. 🍎📚

Four years ago today, the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, stripping a constitutional right from millions. As the consequences continue to grow, I’m fighting for reproductive freedom with @ReproCaucus, and I’ve introduced the ROBE Act because #SCOTUS needs term limits.

Congrats to Bill Heiser on his selection as the next Superintendent of @BaltCoPS. Dr. Heiser brings decades of experience and a deep commitment to student success and support for our educators. Wishing him the best as he steps into this new role with BCPS.
When Trump said, "I don't think about Americans' financial situation,” he meant it. His war, tariffs, and economic policies have made your Summer more expensive.

E000301.text: After the Women at the Service Academies roundtable, I spoke with Dr. Jeannette Gaudry – a proud @NavalAcademy Class of ‘98 graduate – about her takeaways from the conversation and how to keep this momentum for our future servicewomen. Here’s what she had to say:

On June 28th, 2018, a gunman tragically killed five members of our hometown newspaper, the Capital Gazette. Yet, eight years later, I – and so many in our community – am still asking a simple question: what progress have we made in preventing this tragedy from happening again? Congress has a responsibility to rise above thoughts and prayers, which is why I urged my colleagues to return to our collective responsibility to bring about action and commonsense solutions so Annapolis and every community is safe from the epidemic of gun violence.

One of the perks of being so close to D.C. is bringing young people to our nation’s capitol! This week, Sophie, an incredible PhD student and Howard County native, joined us in Washington to talk about her environmental research and how she can continue advocating for her passions – she even got to see some of the work of the House Natural Resources Committee firsthand!

It’s never too early to be civically engaged, and the incredible Howard County high schoolers interning with my friend @katiefryhester are perfect examples of that! I sat down with these students to hear about everything they're working on, including AI regulation policy, and how I can support that work in Washington. There’s no one better to hear from on challenges of the future than the next generation leaders.

11 years ago today, the Supreme Court made a landmark ruling in Obergefell v. Hodges – legalizing same-sex marriage and forever changing the direction of our nation. When James Obergefell and John Arthur flew from Ohio to Maryland to get legally married, they paved the way for the future of equality in our country. As a proud member of the @EqualityCaucus, I will continue fighting for LGBTQ+ rights and the acceptance that all our neighbors deserve.

M001232.text: Eleven years ago today, love won.   The Supreme Court's decision in Obergefell v. Hodges affirmed the freedom to marry the person you love. For me and my husband John, who used to serve as Congressman for the district, this victory was deeply personal. Long before the Court's decision, we stood alongside advocates, families, and countless others fighting for marriage equality because we believed every couple deserves the same rights and dignity.   While we celebrate this milestone, the fight for LGBTQ+ equality is not over. I will continue fighting to protect the rights and freedoms of every American. Happy Pride. Love is love, and it will always be worth fighting for.

Four years ago, the Supreme Court’s decision in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization took away a fundamental freedom that millions of Americans had relied on for nearly 50 years. As a mother of four daughters, I believe women—not politicians—should make their own healthcare decisions. This issue is personal to me. Years ago, I suffered an ectopic pregnancy and almost died. I was able to get the care I needed, and every woman deserves that same freedom and access to care. As a proud member of the @ReproCaucus, I will keep fighting to restore reproductive freedom and protect the right to make personal healthcare decisions. I refuse to accept a world where my daughters have fewer rights than I did. Four years after Dobbs, that fight is more important than ever.

The people of Western and Mountain Maryland have made their disapproval of ICE's Detention Warehouse in Washington County clear. While @DHSgov may wish to ignore the people of the Sixth District, we will not be silenced. Read my new letter to DHS, which contains many of my constituents' voices: https://mcclaindelaney.house.gov/media/press-releases/ice-detention-warehouse-rep-mcclain-delaneys-constituents-speak-out-public

As Congresswoman for Maryland’s Sixth District, I am committed to keeping my constituents informed about the work I’m doing in Washington and across our region. In my latest newsletter, I share updates on newly available disaster relief for our farmers, efforts to fight back against President Trump’s ego-branding of our national treasures, and celebrations with our communities commemorating Juneteenth as we look ahead to America’s 250th birthday. Read more and sign up today: https://iqconnect.house.gov/iqextranet/view_newsletter.aspx?id=101167

On this Father’s Day, I’m grateful for all the dads who lead with love and support. I’m especially blessed to have @JohnDelaney, a wonderful husband and father to our four daughters, and a proud grandpa to Charlie. I’m also thinking of my dad, Thomas, who always believed in me; my father-in-law, Jack, who cherished every moment with family; and my son-in-law, Nick, who loves my daughter Summer and Charlie so dearly. Today, we celebrate the fathers and father figures who shape our lives and strengthen our families. Wishing everyone a Happy Father’s Day!

B001321.text: The Great American Healthcare Plan is about empowering Americans to take control of their own health care and live healthier lives. I was proud to help introduce this bill with @RepEricBurlison to finally take on the status quo that is increasingly pricing Americans out of quality, reliable health care.

I had a great time welcoming Selena and her family to Washington this week to see her winning art piece hung in the halls of the U.S. Capitol! Congratulations again on winning the 2026 Congressional Art Competition.

We cannot rely on dangerous foreign adversaries like China for the drone technology our military and law enforcement agencies use to keep us safe. Today, I introduced legislation with @RepPatHarrigan to restore America's leadership and make sure this technology is being manufactured right here in the United States. https://barrett.house.gov/media/blog/boosting-american-drone-manufacturing

Since 1911, City Rescue Mission of Lansing has provided food, shelter, and a safe haven for the most vulnerable people across our community — serving over 2,500 individuals last year alone. I had a great visit to the ministry this week to hear from their incredible staff and volunteers and to thank them for everything they do to help our neighbors get back on their feet.

Did you know Michigan dairy farmers provide more than 7 million gallons of milk to McDonald’s each year? It was great to be in Westphalia on Monday to see firsthand how our local farms are a critical link in this global food supply chain and celebrate the long-standing partnerships in our communities.

M001237.text: Families are being crushed by high housing costs. Democrats and Republicans came together in massive numbers to pass a bill that will lower those costs. And instead of signing it into law, the President is playing political games.
Buying a home can feel impossible for working families. Tonight, the House passed a new bipartisan bill to cut red tape and build a lot more housing across the country.

Theft and scams lead to higher prices for working families & seniors. We can’t let that happen. The House recently passed our bipartisan bill to combat retail crime. It’s time for the Senate to do the same.
Flint and Saginaw showed out at some amazing Juneteenth celebrations on Friday. Thank you to the organizers for bringing everyone together.

M001234.text: So let me get this straight… Vice President Vance is saying that the level of corruption in this administration makes Watergate look like child’s play? That’s not the flex he thinks it is.
In the richest country in the history of the world, more than half of people should be able to afford health care.

Since Roe v. Wade was overturned 4 years ago today, women have fewer rights than their grandmothers did. We should be doing everything we can to support women and their health care - not attack them. For four years, women have been denied life-saving health care and stripped of the fundamental right to make decisions about their health care and about their own bodies. This is personal for me. As the only pro-choice OB-GYN in Congress, it's enraging to me to know that women across the country are being denied care, having their health and future fertility potentially harmed, and even dying because of it. I want to be clear: I will never stop working to defend your health and your ability to do what's best for you and your family.
HUGE!!!! THIS is why we invest in science!

B001324.text: As June comes to a close, I want to wish everyone a happy Immigrant Heritage Month. America is a nation built by immigrants, and I could not be more grateful for all of their contributions to our country and its culture.

Great meeting with constituent advocates from the @CF_Foundation this week. Thank you for sharing your stories. Know that you’ll always have a partner in me in the fight for health research, resources, and funding.
Huge congratulations to our 2026 Congressional Art Competition winner, Kaylynn. It was a pleasure showing you around the Capitol yesterday…way to represent MO-01! 👏🏾🎨

RT by @RepPatHarrigan: Chinese drone monopoly put on notice amid concerns over CCP spying: 'Strategic mistake' Rep. Pat Harrigan, R-N.C., is spearheading a legislative push to phase out Chinese-manufactured drones currently utilized by U.S. law enforcement agencies. Harrigan argues that relying on systems built by companies linked to the Chinese Communist Party, while simultaneously allowing China to dominate the global drone market, is a critical "strategic mistake." His proposed American Drone Manufacturing Dominance Act of 2026 provides an off-ramp for agencies to replace Chinese-made drones and mandates that federal grant funding be contingent on avoiding foreign-made drone acquisitions after Jan. 1, 2027. The legislation currently allocates $1.5 billion—sourced from Section 301 tariffs—to accelerate the removal of adversarial drones and to heavily subsidize a robust domestic manufacturing base with defense applications. Highlighting their growing sophistication and deployment in overseas conflicts, Harrigan emphasized that the proliferation of foreign drones presents a clear and present national security issue. He pointed to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine as undeniable proof that drones have evolved from a niche capability into a foundational element of modern warfare. Despite operational restrictions in major U.S. cities and highly restricted airspaces like Washington, D.C., domestic drone usage has surged, particularly in border security operations requiring the monitoring of expansive territories. This surge aligns with a 2020 internal memorandum from then-U.S. Border Patrol Chief Rodney Scott, which stated that unmanned technologies offer unprecedented detection and response efficiencies. Currently, local law enforcement remains deeply reliant on Chinese manufacturers like Da Jiang Innovations (DJI); in Texas, for instance, 879 of the 966 drones registered to police and sheriff’s departments were produced by DJI. Acknowledging that the demand for drones will only continue to expand, Harrigan insists that lawmakers must prioritize American safety by forcefully backing domestic manufacturing. He stated that if drones are to remain central to national security, public safety, and critical infrastructure, the United States must retain the capability to build them at home. It currently remains unclear when Harrigan’s bill will be brought to the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives for consideration. https://www.foxnews.com/politics/chinese-drone-monopoly-put-notice-concerns-ccp-spying-strategic-mistake

K000403.text: R to @RepMikeKennedy: For the latest on active fires visit https://utah-fire-info-utahdnr.hub.arcgis.com/

I woke up this morning with the same heavy heart I have carried all week as wildfires continue to burn throughout Utah. This week we lost three firefighters. I am praying for their families and for every Utahn affected. I am grateful for the first responders working around the clock. May God bless and protect them. This should not be our every summer. I represent a district that has watched fire tear through its communities. I have seen what it does to our land. I have met with the ranchers, the land managers, and the state officials who have lived this season after season. Changing the status quo surrounding wildfires is one of my top priorities in Congress. Our communities need forests that are actively managed and a federal government that understands our land and its unique needs. Please stay alert. Check on your neighbors. Support the men and women on the front lines. That is the Utah spirit. It is the reason we get through this year after year.

Ce matin à Vélizy-Villacoublay, aux côtés du Maire et des équipes du Centre communal d'action sociale, j’ai voulu saluer la mobilisation exemplaire de nos services publics pour les plus vulnérables, en particulier nos aînés. Dans le contexte que nous traversons, l’engagement concret de nos agents, leurs appels réguliers, leur accompagnement, les transports solidaires, les livraisons de repas, incarnent pleinement la cohésion et la solidarité qui font une Nation. Je remercie toutes celles et ceux qui, partout sur notre territoire, soignent, protègent et accompagnent : personnels de santé, services de secours, forces de sécurité, agents publics, élus et acteurs associatifs. À chaque instant, continuons d’être vigilants, solidaires envers les plus vulnérables. Veillons à appliquer les bons gestes : adapter sa tenue, boire de manière régulière, éviter les efforts en plein soleil et trouver des points de fraîcheur quand c'est possible. Chacun le mesure, nous devons aller plus vite et plus loin pour nous adapter face aux épisodes climatiques que nous connaissons. État, collectivités, citoyens : accélérer est l’affaire de tous. Dans ces moments, notre responsabilité est claire : protéger, anticiper et agir avec solidarité.
